patch_description:
Builds directly on the best-performing prior seed (global shared RY + RZ rotations with a triple-shell CRZ entangler reusing theta_rz, which scored 0.61 with only 2 distinct circuit parameters) while incorporating the recommended enhancement of adding a single shared global RX layer to unlock a third independent local-rotation axis. The previous experiment that tried to overload one shared angle across mixed-axis (CRZ+CRX) entangling gates on the same wire pairs collapsed to chance-level accuracy (0.50) — likely due to a destructive symmetry/cancellation between the two axis-different two-qubit gates sharing an identical angle on the same pairs across 3 repeated blocks. This design avoids that failure mode entirely: entangling gates remain single-axis (CRZ only, reusing theta_rz, exactly as in the proven-good seed), and the new RX layer is a purely single-qubit, globally-shared addition that cannot interact destructively with the entangler. This keeps parameter count economical (3 distinct circuit params + 2 readout = 5 total) while giving the state preparation full local SU(2)-like coverage (RX+RY+RZ) before entanglement, which should improve worst-group margin and generalization without reintroducing the observed instability.

Key insights:
1. Proven structure (global RY/RZ + shared CRZ triple-shell entangler) is preserved verbatim since it is empirically the best-performing candidate so far.
2. Only ADD to it, never remix axes on the same wires with a shared angle across different gate types — that was the root cause of the catastrophic collapse in the current program.
3. A single new globally-shared RX parameter cheaply adds a third rotation axis, which recommendations flagged as a promising, minimal-risk expressivity boost.
4. Parameter count is kept as low as justified (3 distinct circuit params) to respect the strong parameter-economy scoring term.
